solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old society girl with mad somersaulting seriously injured?

indicators.note: a somersault turns you head over heels, so the joined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, was a young woman entering high society
bats is informal for crazy

explanation.surface: An old-time debutante, together with a crazy acrobat, tumbling about.
explanation.walkthrough: DEB plus BATS is DEBBATS, which read backwards gives STABBED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stabbed has been wounded with a blade, a serious injury; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Food provided by Christian group entertaining prophet

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your home, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A church charity serves refreshments while hosting a visiting preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian group' suggests a congregation, but crosswords use it for the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried Indian pastry with a spiced filling, an example of food.

clue.text: A short course for goddess

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
a starter is the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: A brief training programme suited to a divine being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a class or route, but it is a course of a meal, the starter, docked of its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician deity of fertility and love, so she is a goddess.

clue.text: One may need skill interrupting a drunken spree?

definitions.text: One may need skill interrupting a drunken spree?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a bender is a heavy drinking session
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Breaking up a boozy night out takes some talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the person serving drinks needs skill when a spree gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves at a bar, and handling drinkers on a binge calls for tact and craft.

clue.text: To chop down trees on site affords redeveloping

indicators.note: redeveloping a plot means rebuilding it in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A building plot gets cleared of its woodland when developers move in.
explanation.definitionFit: To disafforest is to clear land of forest, i.e. fell its trees.

clue.text: Kitchen item in British Library?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a library is something that lends books

explanation.surface: Asking whether a kitchen gadget is kept in the British Library.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a library is being described loosely as a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is an electric appliance for liquidising food, found in a kitchen.

clue.text: Vehicle taking Oxbridge sportspeople regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: Blues are sportspeople who have represented Oxford or Cambridge; every other letter of that word is kept

explanation.surface: Transport laid on for the university teams.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson who has competed against the other university; alternate letters of BLUES give BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Stopped losing head and relaxed

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's first letter is dropped

parts.note: ceased means stopped

explanation.surface: Someone stopped worrying and calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased is a synonym of loosened or relaxed, as when tension is eased.

clue.text: One may be troubled, somehow not trustful ultimately

definitions.text: One may be troubled, somehow not trustful ultimately

indicators.note: somehow suggests it is done in some unspecified way, so the letters are reordered
not means without, so the following letter is left out of the word

parts.note: the word taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone worried who, in the end, just cannot trust.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L, the last letter of trustful, out of TROUBLED and rearrange TROUBED. The whole clue also describes a doubter: a troubled person who does not trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter is a sceptic, someone uncertain who withholds belief or trust.

clue.text: Anger about traditional fashion industry

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: rage is fury or anger
trad is short for traditional, as in trad jazz

explanation.surface: Fury at the old-fashioned ways of the clothing business.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal name for the clothing and garment business.

clue.text: It's damp across hill before hint of sun for travellers

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one piece stretches around the other

parts.note: moist means damp
a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

indicators.note: a hint is only a trace, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Weather report: drizzle over the hills before sunshine, good news for those travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' belongs to the wordplay: the thing that is damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists are drivers, people who travel by car.

clue.text: Being injured is shock, little good

parts.note: to stun is to shock
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Getting hurt comes as a shock and does little good.
explanation.definitionFit: Stung means hurt by a sting, or figuratively wounded, so it describes having been injured.

clue.text: Material offered by officer putting worker off

indicators.note: putting something off removes it, so one word is taken out of the other

parts.note: a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer
a worker ant, the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: Cloth issued by a military officer who has sent a labourer away.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ANT from SERGEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric, used for uniforms, so it is a material.

clue.text: Fur trade's arranged by this dodgy dealer

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady trader has organised a deal in pelts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraudster is a cheat or swindler, someone who deals dishonestly.

clue.text: Feat of a Greek character — this writer participating in festival. say

indicators.note: a participant is in the thick of an event, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a festival is an example of an event, signalled by say
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: A Greek man performs a feat while the setter joins in at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter speaking of themselves, a standard crossword way to clue the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: An achievement is something accomplished through effort, a synonym of feat.

clue.text: A hot toddler we'd rocked to get asleep

indicators.note: rocked means shaken to and fro, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Parents rocking an overheated child until it nods off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead to the world is an idiom for being fast asleep and unaware of anything.

clue.text: Wife suffering is rolling round

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
to suffer can mean to permit, as in 'suffer the little children'

explanation.surface: A wife in pain is writhing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' looks like pain, but it is the old sense of tolerating or permitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallowing means rolling about, as a pig does in mud.

clue.text: Liven up, being at home with whisky?

parts.note: being in means being at home
whisky is a spirit

explanation.surface: Cheering yourself up by staying in with a dram.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks whisky as an example of a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspirit is to fill with spirit, encourage or animate someone.

clue.text: An imaginary heaven? Do not, do not come down to earth

parts.note: never is a strong do not, given twice
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A paradise that isn't real, so stop daydreaming and come back to reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Never-never land, from Peter Pan, is an imaginary ideal place, a fantasy paradise.

clue.text: Ruling from some clever dictator

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters are taken from within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A judgement handed down by a shrewd despot.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is a decision or ruling, especially a jury's finding.

clue.text: Chemical substance picked up in nocturnal journey

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a trip after dark

explanation.surface: Something toxic detected during an overnight trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a compound of nitrogen with another element, a chemical substance.

clue.text: Gets hold of Government's original files

indicators.note: the original is what comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
rasps are coarse files for shaping wood or metal

explanation.surface: Someone seizes the official government documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Files' looks like documents, but it is the tools.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to seize or grip firmly, so grasps means takes hold of.

clue.text: Very good Las Vegas game, but learner's missed out in spin

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword slang for very good

indicators.note: something missed out is left out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: roulette is a casino game
L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A gambler does well at the Vegas tables, though the novice has lost out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' could be many words; in crosswords PI, short for pious, is the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a spin on one foot in ballet.

clue.text: Decree establishing four nations as one ultimately

parts.note: the United Kingdom is made up of four nations
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the word's closing letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A law unifying the home nations as a single state.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK's four nations are England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict of the Russian tsar, so any arbitrary decree.

clue.text: Beast, cad — no leader

indicators.note: without a leader the word loses its front letter

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, an old word for a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Calling someone an animal and a bounder with nobody in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a fish-eating river mammal, so a beast.

clue.text: Picture not showing wine next to a dish

indicators.note: not showing means kept out of sight, so that word is removed

parts.note: a portrait is a picture of a person
port is a fortified wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painting that leaves the wine out of the still life beside a plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove PORT from PORTRAIT and add A.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs.

clue.text: People in excellent matches — provisions for spectators say?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
men are people
ties are matches in a competition, as in cup ties

explanation.surface: Fans at top fixtures and the facilities laid on for them.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a knockout match in British football, so ties are matches. The question mark flags spectators as only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful facilities, such as toilets or seating laid on for a crowd at a ground.

clue.text: Big woman here in matrimonial crime? Little woman!

indicators.note: the woman is what is left here in the longer word once the stated part is taken away

parts.note: bigamy is marrying while still married to someone else
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large lady involved in a marriage offence, though she is described as small.
explanation.walkthrough: BIGAMY is BIG followed by a woman: take away BIG to leave her.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.

clue.text: Baby with nappy not right wobbling about?

indicators.note: not right means without the abbreviation for right, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a terry is a towelling nappy, the British word for a diaper

explanation.surface: A toddler with no proper nappy staggering around.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Rs in the nappy word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means unsteady on one's feet, inclined to wobble.

clue.text: Hair concealing one grand female — a beastly type

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
I is the Roman numeral one
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A woman's hair hiding a large sum, and she is a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: I and G go inside TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, a wild animal, and figuratively a fierce woman.
